raw_segments.text: And now, oh, my judges, I desire to prove to you that the real philosopher has reason
to be of good cheer when he is about to die, and that after death he may hope to obtain
the greatest good in the other world.
And how this may be, simias and sibis, I will endeavor to explain.
For I deem that the true votary of philosophy is likely to be misunderstood by other men.
They do not perceive that he is always pursuing death and dying.
And if this be so, and he has had the desire of death all his life long, why, when his
time comes, should he repine at that which he has been always pursuing and desiring?
